name: A Baying of Gnolls
summary: Gnolls raid Verner Osgood’s stable in Lakeshire from the Redridge foothills. Blackrock orcs already threaten the region, and Verner asks travelers to drive off the brutes and mystics endangering his horses.

sections.title: Horses on the Ridge
sections.body: Verner Osgood’s stable in Lakeshire has become dangerous to run. Blackrock orcs hold the heights, and gnoll packs roam the ridges around town. Gnoll raiders have reached the northern edge of Verner’s paddocks, preying on horses that wander too close to the bluffs.

sections.title: A Coordinated Menace
sections.body: Gnoll packs north of Lakeshire bring both brute force and primitive spellcraft. Their brutes overwhelm prey while mystics wield wild magic. Thinning their numbers gives the settlement a brief respite, but their aggression points to a greater power higher in the hills.

faq.q: Why does Verner Osgood need help with gnolls?
faq.answer: Gnolls from the northern ridges have begun reaching Verner’s stables and snatching horses that stray from the paddocks. With Blackrock orcs also threatening the region, he cannot protect his stock alone.
Redridge brutes and mystics prowl the elevated ridges and foothills directly north and east of Lakeshire, overlooking the town and the road toward the Everstill Bridge.

faq.q: Why are gnolls an issue alongside the Blackrock orcs?
faq.answer: Blackrock orcs are Redridge’s main military threat, and local gnoll packs take advantage of the distraction. Lakeshire’s defenders are stretched thin, and Stormwind sends few reinforcements, leaving the predators free to range up to the village perimeter.

faq.q: What comes after dealing with these gnolls?
aliases: what next after baying of gnolls
faq.answer: After the brutes and mystics are thinned, the howling continues in the hills. It points to a greater leadership threat in the surrounding heights.

Redridge mystics use rudimentary nature and elemental magic, turning erratic, feral incantations against trespassers. Their presence among the brutes suggests an organized clan rather than lone scavengers.

faq.q: Is Stormwind sending soldiers to protect Lakeshire's stables?
faq.answer: No. Stormwind’s royal court has left Redridge largely to defend itself amid political turmoil and troop shortages. Magistrate Solomon and citizens like Verner Osgood must recruit wandering adventurers.

angles.text: Stormwind’s neglect strains small communities across the southern kingdom. Tradesmen like Verner must hire private help to protect essential supply lines.
As a hunter, you face wild beasts and feral packs in Redridge that have grown bold without organized culls. They threaten domestic animals and travelers.
